documents.title: University of Wyoming syllabus template with sample AI language
tiers: Option 2: Use only with prior permission
Option 4: Use is freely permitted with no acknowledgement
documents.summary: A university syllabus template from Academic Affairs that recommends every syllabus carry an AI section near the academic dishonesty statement. It supplies four sample statements, adapted from the University of Delaware, ranging from prohibition to free use, and leaves the choice to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The template only "recommend[s] that faculty include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use" and offers four sample options (prohibited, prior permission, acknowledgement, freely permitted). It sets no single university rule and leaves the choice to instructors, so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The template says "We recommend that faculty include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use in each of their syllabi", a recommendation to instructors to state AI rules in the syllabus. It fits P09 (syllabus statement); it is a "recommend", so modality is should and it is not a mandate.
units.anchor: include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use in each of their syllabi
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P09, should, instructor, before-course. Source: "We recommend that faculty include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use in each of their syllabi". No disagreement.

units.why: The same passage places the AI section "generally in the location of their Student Academic Dishonesty statement", a placement suggestion for communicating expectations; it is part of the syllabus-statement practice so P09 with a fit note.
units.anchor: generally in the location of their Student Academic Dishonesty statement
units.fit_note: Adds where in the syllabus the AI section goes (next to the academic dishonesty statement), which the type does not name.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The source says the AI section goes "generally in the location of their Student Academic Dishonesty statement", a real placement recommendation to instructors; kept as P09 with B's fit_note, should, course-start.

units.why: The sentence "it is important that faculty clearly communicate their expectations of course collaboration policies (with other students)" asks instructors to state collaboration rules alongside the AI statement. P09 is the nearest type (state expectations in the syllabus), but it concerns peer collaboration, not AI itself.
units.anchor: it is important that faculty clearly communicate their expectations of course collaboration policies
units.fit_note: The type is about stating AI expectations; this asks for collaboration-with-students policies to be stated in the same place as the AI section. Coder B's note: concerns communicating collaboration-with-peers expectations, not only AI expectations.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P09, should, instructor, course-start. Source: "it is important that faculty clearly communicate their expectations of course collaboration policies (with other students) in this same area". No change; fit_notes merged.

units.why: "We offer the following language as draft material ... that instructors may want to consider" shows the university supplies sample syllabus wording for instructors to adopt, which is exactly P110 (sample language and templates).
units.anchor: We offer the following language as draft material
units.policy: The university offers draft AI syllabus language, adapted from University of Delaware, that instructors may want to consider.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P110 and admin/before-course but A said informs and B said may. Source: "We offer the following language as draft material ... that instructors may want to consider". The university is stating that it offers material, not granting itself permission; the 'may' belongs to instructors. So informs, with A's normalized policy, which matches the passage.

units.why: Four options (prohibited, prior permission, acknowledgement, free use) are offered for instructors to pick from, "instructors may want to consider"; the point is that the choice is left to each instructor, so P04 rather than a default stance.
units.anchor: that instructors may want to consider
units.policy: Instructors choose among four sample AI syllabus options (use prohibited; use only with prior permission; use only with acknowledgement; use freely permitted).
units.fit_note: The document sets no rule itself; it only offers options, so the decision per course sits with the instructor.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this as P04; B folded it into a fit_note on the tiers unit. Source: "that instructors may want to consider" with four alternative options, so the choice is left to each instructor. This is a distinct rule from naming the tiers (P05), so kept as a separate unit.

units.why: The four options are a named ladder of AI-use levels from "Use prohibited" to "Use is freely permitted with no acknowledgement", so P05 (named tiers) fits. P04 is separately coded for the delegation to instructors; here the point is the tier structure.
units.anchor: Option 2: Use only with prior permission
units.policy: The sample language defines four named levels of AI use: Option 1 use prohibited, Option 2 use only with prior permission, Option 3 use only with acknowledgement, Option 4 use freely permitted with no acknowledgement.
units.fit_note: The four options are sample statements an instructor may pick, so the choice is also left to the instructor (P04).
units.resolution_why: Both coded P05 with actor instructor. Phase: A course-start, B before-course; modality: A informs, B may. Source: Options 1-4 are headed sample statements. They define levels of AI use, a fact about the template (informs), and are prepared for instructors when designing the syllabus (before-course). The instructor's freedom to pick is coded separately as P04. Normalized policy from A kept.

units.why: Option 1 states "Students are not permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course", a flat ban on AI on graded work, so P01.
units.anchor: Students are not permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools
units.frag_start: Students are not permitted to use
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P01, student, during-work, must-not. Source: "Students are not permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course." No disagreement.

units.why: Option 1 adds "Each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools", which equates automated tools with other people helping. P45 is the nearest type; P19 does not fit because it bars having AI produce submitted work, whereas this bars substantive assistance generally.
units.anchor: complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools
units.fit_note: Treats automated tools like other people under a no-substantive-assistance rule rather than naming a collaboration or citation policy. Coder B coded P19 and noted the phrasing covers assistance from people and automated tools alike.
units.resolution_why: A coded P45, B coded P19. Source: "Each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools." The sentence does not say AI may not generate submitted work; it puts automated tools on the same footing as help from other people under an unassisted-work rule. That is P45's definition (AI treated like a human collaborator or outside source), so P45. The outright AI ban is the preceding sentence (P01).

units.why: Option 2 says AI tools are allowed "if instructor permission is obtained in advance", so AI is permitted only after explicit prior approval; this is P107 (prior approval) and not P10 (asking when unsure).
units.anchor: if instructor permission is obtained in advance
units.frag_start: Students are permitted to use advanced
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and policy type. Source supports the codes as written in why.

units.why: Option 2 continues "Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools", a fallback that applies when no permission was given, so P06.
units.anchor: Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and policy type. Source supports the codes as written in why.

units.why: Option 3 lets students use the tools "if that use is properly documented and credited", so AI use is conditional on attribution; P24 (disclose AI use with each submission).
units.anchor: if that use is properly documented and credited
units.frag_start: Students are permitted to use advanced
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and policy type. Source supports the codes as written in why.

units.why: The example citation "Chat-GPT-3. (YYYY, Month DD of query). “Text of your query.” Generated using OpenAI." requires the tool, date and query text in the citation, which is P25.
units.anchor: text generated using ChatGPT-3 should include a citation such as
units.policy: Text generated with an AI tool should include a citation giving the tool, the date of the query, the text of the query and the provider; material from other tools should follow a similar citation convention.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P25, student, during-work, should. A wrote a normalized policy and B left it null with the closing sentence as anchor. Source: "text generated using ChatGPT-3 should include a citation such as ..." and "Material generated using other tools should follow a similar citation convention." The anchor alone does not cover the tool/date/query content, so A's normalized policy is kept.

units.why: Option 4 says students "are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course; no special documentation or citation is required", an open default permission, so P02.
units.anchor: no special documentation or citation is required
units.frag_start: Students are permitted to use advanced
units.policy: Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course; no special documentation or citation is required.
units.fit_note: Also states that no disclosure is needed (the opposite of P24).
units.resolution_why: Both coded P02, permit, may, student. B added a disclosure-citation topic and a fit_note that the option waives disclosure; source says "no special documentation or citation is required", so both are kept. A's normalized policy matches the source.

notes: Only AI text is one paragraph plus four options in a long syllabus template; the template academic-dishonesty example does not mention AI and was not coded. The Option 1 and 2 no-substantive-assistance sentences were coded as P45 (with fit_note) and P06 respectively. | Only one included document; AI content is a single section of a syllabus template. Sample options are templates, so unit-level modalities describe the sample wording.
